#139596. "I'm betting on the sickos" - Signet City aims to 'expand the scope of RPGs' by drawing on the success of Citizen Sleeper

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2520 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Eurogamer ↗ Open Full Page

"I'm betting on the sickos" - Signet City aims to 'expand the scope of RPGs' by drawing on the success of Citizen Sleeper

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When I last spoke to Citizen Sleeper creator Gareth Damian Martin, it was on the eve of Citizen Sleeper 2's release.
  • It has been revealed that "I feel a certain responsibility that comes with success," Damian Martin - also known by their studio name Jump Over the Age - told me at the time.
  • Industry observers note that they wanted the definition of RPGs to be "expanded", to make them as varied as "rich and varied" as tabletop RPGs can be.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When I last spoke to Citizen Sleeper creator Gareth Damian Martin, it was on the eve of Citizen Sleeper 2's release. Like its predecessor, the game was a critical hit, cementing Damian Martin's reputation as one of the most successful independent game developers around. But they weren't content. They wanted to do more, to push more, to stretch the idea of what a role-playing video game could be.

It has been revealed that "I feel a certain responsibility that comes with success," Damian Martin - also known by their studio name Jump Over the Age - told me at the time. "I feel lots of things about this medium, and I feel if I'm in the one percent of indie developers - and the even smaller percent of solo developers - who manage to make something and have that thing be successful, then I have responsibility towards putting things into the industry and into the world that contribute somehow to whatever I think the industry should be doing.".

Industry observers note that they wanted the definition of RPGs to be "expanded", to make them as varied as "rich and varied" as tabletop RPGs can be. Citizen Sleeper was a step towards realising that goal but even it had limitations, which is why Damian Martin has returned to take things a step further with their next game Signet City. Announced during this year's somewhat samey-feeling Summer Game Fest, it's a startlingly original work.

Industry observers note that signet City was enigmatic. Revealed in a cinematic trailer, it was black and white, bleak, thick-lined, smoggy, and dirty; choked in industrial decay and brimming with post-punk non-conformance. It was also first-person, a notable change for Damian Martin, whose games have, up until now, been zoomed out and abstracted. Most eye-catching of all, though, was the descriptor "fungalpunk" - a game in which we'd play as a parasite in someone's mind. As far as expanding the scope of RPGs goes: "100 percent that is exactly what I'm trying to do here," Gareth Damian Martin tells me now.

We talk in a video call in the immediate aftermath of Signet City's announcement - apologies for not writing this until Not-GTA Week, though what an opportunity that presented - and Damian Martin is as calm and eloquent and thoughtful as ever, nestled in a compact office decorated with collages of their current influences. This room looked different when we spoke about Citizen Sleeper 1, looked different when we spoke about Citizen Sleeper 2, and it looks different again now. Damian Martin is a visual person, as someone with a visual design background would be.

With Signet City only just announced, questions abound. The announcement trailer doesn't reveal much (not much has come out since, either), but we do know it takes place in the North of England in the 80s. It's a setting I'm not sure we've ever had in games, and one that's woefully overlooked in entertainment in general, barring BBC TV demonstrates like Our Friends in the North and Boys from the Blackstuff, which Damian Martin directly references. We know there are themes like industrial decay, welded as they are to that time and place. But there's been no talk of how the game plays, or what being a parasite in someone's mind means.

After speaking with Damian Martin, I've got a much better idea. But first, to the beginning. Signet City is an idea they've had floating around their head for a very long time. This was the game they pitched to their publisher Fellow Traveller after Citizen Sleeper 1 came out, but decided to hold in favour of making Citizen Sleeper 2 - a decision driven partly by a desire "to build myself a bigger platform" to launch a newly introduced game idea from. The idea originated in a very unexpected place: the musician Sting. Damian Martin was doing theatre design for Sting's musical show The Last Ship before they became a full-time game-maker (go back even further in Damian Martin's life and you'll find a degree in puppetry there). They had to research Newcastle in the 1980s because of it. The Last Ship is about Sting's upbringing in Wallsend, a town near Newcastle, in the wake of a shipyard being closed there - the town's source of sustenance. And it was while working on the project that the 80s imprinted on Damian Martin's mind.

"I was looking at these pictures of these massive gleaming ships hanging over the top of little terraced houses," they say, "and this conflict between time periods and ideas of society, and I remember thinking at the time: that was science-fiction somehow. When you look at those images, it could be a spaceship; that ship that's being built in Newcastle might as well be a spaceship, especially science-fiction of the 80s - a lot of it was about that.

"It just stuck in my brain and I started to work up this fictional 1980s British city that would be in that period of de-industrialisation and social change," they continue. "But would be based on a completely different kind of industrial background and have this weird kind of fungalpunk technology layered into it. So that's been sitting around in my head for almost 10 years slowly accruing material and reference points and things.".

According to recent reports, fungalpunk: there's that word again, but what does it mean? I've heard of cyberpunk and steampunk, not that I could tell you easily what they mean, but I've never heard of fungapunk - I don't think anyone has. Thankfully, in this case, it's fairly literal. "You are fungal in a very true sense," Damian Martin states. You are a fungal parasite and there are themes of decay and reinvigoration, things fungi are closely tied to. One of the phrases Damian Martin has been using as a north star for the project - something they do on all of their projects - is the idea of being "a fungal superhero", which makes me giggle. I've definitely not heard that before either.

Recent findings suggest that it's an idea inspired by a 1989 Japanese film called Tetsuo: The Iron Man - about a salary man who's slowly turning into metal - that Damian Martin adores. "I love it so much," they say. "It's an amazing movie, a beautiful movie, and really strange. And so I wanted to do something that was in that vibe. The way that that film commits to the idea of a body becoming metal and the visceral kind of strangeness of that. I wanted to do something that was about humans and becoming fungal; which we already are, we already have lots of bits of bacteria and fungal nail infections - we are multitudes.".

It has been revealed that the punk side of the equation is, again, fairly literal. It refers to the post-punk cultural and musical scene at the time. The scene is often overshadowed by the brasher, more aggressive punk movement, but it's one that's just as anti-establishment, albeit in perhaps in a deeper, darker, more nihilistic way. Think Joy Division referencing novelist JG Ballard in its songs, for example. "Post-punk was this engagement with structural politics and transgressive fiction and all kinds of interesting big ideas getting into pop culture through music," Damian Martin says.

Recent findings suggest that now watch the game's trailer again; you can feel all these things oozing through it. The aesthetic, the music, the setting. There are also massive clues - although they're not obvious - about how the game plays. We see the start of a character called Sid's story in the trailer, who's one of the hosts we can inhabit in the game. We choose an area of the city we want to play in, then drop into a person's head who lives or operates there. And in Sid's case, she wakes up in a river just as we - the parasite - wake in her mind. Twins!

Recent findings suggest that we control Sid as we would a character in another first-person game - Dishonored or Skyrim are two examples Damian Martin uses - and we see a bit of this in the trailer. What we don't see are any other mechanics, which are, once more, dice rolls related to skills, as in Citizen Sleeper. In order to do something in the world that isn't insignificantly easy, we need to roll a dice and add modifiers to see if we can achieve it.

In a recent development, "So the way it works is you drop into someone's head for the day. Let's say we drop into this worker's head for the day and we want to get to a certain part of the city, and let's say we need to kick down a door to get there," says Damian Martin. "Well, we're going to have to make this character really angry to get them to kick down that door, so we're going to maybe get them in an argument with some other fellow workers, and maybe we're going to choose to provoke that argument and then they'll get really angry. Then that will have narrative effects, but also it will have mechanical effects in the sense of, like, okay, now we have a modifier that makes physical strength more powerful, so we can do these physical strength actions.".

Skills are tied to a person's emotions, intriguingly, and your job as the parasite is to find things that affect these emotions so you can amplify them and increase your chances of achieving things. Then at the end of the day, all of that emotion gets "extracted out" and becomes a resource you can permanently improve your host's skills with. "So you start to adjust each of your hosts in a direction you think will be helpful for you to do what you need each day in these hub locations," Damian Martin explains. But this has consequences. Push someone towards angry actions and they'll become a more angry person, understandably. "And that will shape their future even when you're no longer controlling them.".

Which begs the question: what exactly does a parasite need to do? What is a parasite's objective in the game? This is an answer Damian Martin isn't quite ready to give, though they do their best to attempt it. "You have your own objectives as a parasite," they say. "You don't have an objective like: this is your mission, parasite. But there are some bigger offers coming to you through your sensorium, through your experience of voices and attractions and tastes and smells, that are leading you in different places as a parasite. That's your objective, to grow and gain power, although to what end you don't initially know.".

Sources indicate that it's in this parasitical difference Signet City starts to stand apart. For starters, it's just appealing weird to be a parasite, though as Damian Martin muses, aren't we often parasites in relation to characters in tabletop role-playing games? "We push them around; sometimes we talk for them and sometimes we listen to them; sometimes we use our name and sometimes we use their name." Here, it's simply out in the open. "I wanted to create an RPG where I acknowledged and then also played that into the fiction," they say.

Sources indicate that being in a thing in someone's mind allows a host character autonomy, to a degree, so they can have their own motivations and stories and struggles besides yours. They don't have to be thoughtless mannequins awaiting our direction. Dropping into their minds allows us to drop straight into a tense scenario. "Stories for me that are very exciting in fiction and literature are stories about people who are in it," Damian Martin notes. "They're in the situation already, they're in the shit, they're having to deal with everything.".

The ability to read their minds also lets us know them more intimately than we know characters in other games, who usually, you know, need to speak to us in order for us to understand them. It also circumvents the need for an NPC to suddenly and unnaturally open up to you about their lives, the first moment they meet you, and to provide you with "a neatly packaged challenge". That's not needed here. "The core relationships of the game are actually between you and your hosts," Damian Martin says.

Industry observers note that there's a layer that exists on top of the character's thoughts where the parasite lives and functions - a layer of feelings and emotions and sensory reactions to a world outside. A hopefully quite bizarre and alien layer, which presents challenges of its own, because how do you describe the experiences of a parasite in someone's mind? "What does it feel like to be a parasite and how do I make that comprehensible to a human?" Damian Martin wonders. They are good questions I can't wait to experience the answers to.

But when will that be? There's no release date yet, and when we talked in the summer, Signet City was only halfway through development. It was confirmed early partly to make sure people understood it wasn't Citizen Sleeper 3, and partly because people could probably use some time to sit with the idea for a bit and digest it. "We can't just drop it all on everyone's heads," Damian Martin claims, "because I think the potential for it being misunderstood or just ignored is high.".

Sources indicate that and that's a telling admission for a project which has been characterised by Damian Martin multiple times as a risk - as even "the biggest swing I have ever taken". They seemed genuinely nervous about announcing it, though some of those nerves were subsiding by the time we talked. They're not entirely gone, mind you. There's a lingering awareness that Signet City is newly introduced and different enough that people might not gel with it, though that's the price of pushing at boundaries, I suppose.

"What worries me more," Damian Martin claims, "is have I still got it? Am I able to produce things that are appealing and exciting to people just based on my own tastes and obsessions and interests? When it comes to announcing something like Signet City, that's what makes me really nervous - more than industry, more than money, more than anything. Is this actually interesting?".

Of course, it's easy for me to say they shouldn't worry. It's exciting when a game blares as loudly and uniquely as Signet City did during Summer Game Fest, though that is obviously no guarantee it'll find an audience. But I think it will. I'm convinced there are more people like me who it will appeal to. Gareth Damian Martin is betting on it. "I'm betting on the sickos," they say. "The thing I've learned is that my obsessions are sticky and they stick to other people, and I think there's something in art where we really like to be tourists in other people's obsessions - that's a fun place to be. That's what I'm hoping for.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been nearly three years since Best Buy decided to ditch selling physical copies of movies, stripping its inventory from both its brick-and-mortar stores and its online catalog. But with the growing rise of 4K Blu-ray collections as a vinyl-esque collector’s item, the electronics giant has slowly begun dipping its toes back into the physical media game.

As spotted by TheHDRoom on Twitter and on the 4K Blu-ray subreddit, Best Buy is now selling 14 different 4K Blu-rays on its website, marking another step in the brand’s slow return to selling physical media. These films include:.

Technically, Blu-ray returned to Best Buy’s online storefront in August of 2025, when it opened a third-party marketplace similar to Amazon or Walmart. These titles, however, are shipped and sold by Best Buy. Everything’s still online-only, unfortunately, save for The Odyssey, which debuted in-store shelf displays alongside yesterday’s release date. It shouldn’t come as too much of a surprise that The Odyssey is getting some special treatment; in addition to its status as a box office juggernaut, Nolan’s previous movie, Oppenheimer, initially sold out of physical copies in its first week of release in 2023.

Outside of these 14 titles, additional Blu-rays continue to be sold through Best Buy’s third-party marketplace.

Upgrade, 11/20: Best Buy confirmed to The HD Room on Twitter that The Odyssey is just the first 4K Blu-ray to return to physical locations, as it looks to continue adding “some” Blu-rays back to its stores.

The Odyssey may/will be joined by other 4K UHD titles at Best Buy in the future: "The Odyssey inspired a homecoming of our own – some physical media is returning to Best Buy. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mesh routers are among the hottest-selling types of routers in networking, and leading the charge are products based on the Wi-Fi 7 standard. Mesh routers enable you to fully cover your home or office with wireless coverage that would otherwise be impossible with a single, standalone router.

Fortunately, numerous manufacturers are producing Wi-Fi 7 mesh routers, offering a wide range of options to choose from. If you prefer seamless integration with your Amazon account and Alexa services, consider opting for the Eero Pro 7. If you want endless configuration options and no-cost features, such as extensive Parental Controls, the Asus ZenWiFi BT4 has you covered. If you're looking for a delicate balance of performance and features at a bargain price, consider the TP-Link Deco BE95.

According to recent reports, however, one thing to keep in mind when shopping for a network upgrade is that not all Wi-Fi 7 routers are created equal. While there are speed differences between products that depend on several factors (channel width, total number of streams, etc.), the primary differentiator among Wi-Fi 7 routers comes down to the number of supported bands. There are dual- and tri-band routers, with the latter offering the best potential performance. Dual-band routers only support the 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, while tri-band routers support the higher-performing and shorter-range 6 GHz band. The maximum performance of the 6 GHz band is what gives tri-band Wi-Fi 7 routers a significant theoretical speed advantage over their Wi-Fi 6E predecessors.

Some manufacturers, such as Asus, also offer quad-band routers that feature either two 5 GHz wireless bands or two 6 GHz bands.

With that stated, check out the extensive list below for all the best deals on Wi-Fi 7 routers from Asus, Eero, Netgear, MSI, and TP-Link.

It has been revealed that the Asus ZenWiFi BD4 is an entry-level Wi-Fi 7 router and thus only supports two bands (2.4 GHz and 5 GHz). This 3-pack features up to 3.6 Gbps of combined throughput and covers 6,500 square feet.

The Deco BE23 is TP-Link's most entry-level Wi-Fi 7 router, sporting dual-band wireless, up to 3.6 Gbps throughput, and coverage of 4,500 square feet.

The Deco BE63 is a mid-range, tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router with four 2.5 GbE ports, 10 Gbps of combined throughput, and coverage of 5,800 square feet.

The TP-Link Deco 7 Pro BE10000 is a tri-band, Wi-Fi 7 mesh system that includes three wireless nodes. Each node comes with four 2.5 GbE ports, and the total wireless coverage is 7,600 square feet.

TP-Link's flagship Deco BE95 Wi-Fi 7 mesh router supports four bands, delivering up to 33 Gbps of throughput. It also features two 10 GbE ports per node.

Sources indicate that the Eero Pro 7 is a mid-range, tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router that offers coverage of up to 4,000 square feet. Each wireless node features two 5 GbE ports.

The Eero Max 7 is Amazon's flagship Wi-Fi 7 router, featuring tri-band wireless, two 2.5 GbE ports, two 10 GbE ports, and up to 5,000 square feet of coverage.

Sources indicate that the Orbi 770 is the latest in Netgear's long line of Orbi mesh routers. This one is a tri-band system with coverage of up to 5,500 square feet and 11 Gbps of combined throughput. You also get three 2.5 GbE ports and one 2.5 GbE port for WAN.

Sources indicate that MSI's Roamii BE Lite is a newcomer on the Wi-Fi 7 mesh router scene, and it's a dual-band unit. Each node includes 2.5 GbE ports, and MSI even provides wall mounts in the box.

Sources indicate that the MSI Roamii BE Pro is a high-powered, tri-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh router that won't break the bank. Each node includes four 2.5 GbE ports for connecting your wired devices, and the mesh system is controlled by a rather feature-packed smartphone app.

According to recent reports, if you want a high-performance mesh router, look no further. The Asus ZenWiFi BE30000 is a quad-band solution, featuring three wireless nodes. Aggregate speeds across all four bands (you get two 6 GHz bands, one of which is dedicated to a wireless backhaul) are 30 Gbps, and you get coverage for up to 11,000 square feet.

  • The Galaxy Z Fold 8 folds and unfolds like other foldable devices – that much you know.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Folding phones have come in numerous variations over the years as the concept has evolved. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the latest evolution that introduces a form factor that fits every user. Its unique design makes it a foldable most people can actually use – which makes it a perfect gift. You might be surprised by what it can do.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

It’s in the name. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 folds and unfolds like other foldable devices – that much you know. But what the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s form factor provides is something different to what most might be familiar with.

Instead of a tall device that unfolds into a near-uniform square display, you get a wider screen more like a tablet. That makes it perfect for watching videos or movies. Content that naturally works well on TVs or your computer will look great on the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

What about content that’s best viewed in portrait mode? Because it opens up to a tablet-like display, you can turn the Fold 8 to watch YouTube Shorts or Instagram Reels without a problem, so if you or someone you know likes to watch content on a bigger display, the Z Fold 8 makes that much easier. It really doesn’t matter what content you come across – the wider inner display gives you that large screen feeling.

In a recent development, like a well-designed tool, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has more purposes than the tasks best suited for the inner display. That shorter, wider profile makes the outer display smaller, but not as thin as something on other foldables, like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

According to recent reports, in reality, the aspect ratio is similar enough across both the inner and outer screens that most content scales well on the shorter front panel. Social apps like X and Instagram look great because videos and images are able to fill the screen, rather than squeeze. Samsung’s One UI software also supports app optimization across both screens, although the experience may vary by app.

In a recent development, saying the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s outer display is “minimal” isn’t a dig, either. Apps can be refreshing to use when you don’t need to open them on a large scale. Take Messages, for instance. It’s not a complex app, and there isn’t a ton to see – just the last couple of messages exchanged. The same goes for plenty of apps available on the Google Play Store.

Sources indicate that and guess what? If you don’t like using the app on a smaller display, just unfold the phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is such a versatile phone, whether it’s a gift during the holidays or one for yourself.

There are instances where you need the large real estate. One UI 9 gives the Galaxy Z Fold 8 the option to open and run multiple apps on your screen. There are several ways you can do it, too.

The main approach is to split two apps on the wide inner display. But if you want to see more from one app, you can simply drag the split over in one direction. One UI 9 leaves room to add one more app to that split screen, giving you a three-way Split View. All it takes is dragging an app from the taskbar and choosing the spot.

In a recent development, if you truly need a fourth app open, you have the option to open another in a floating window. Having four apps open at once is definitely a niche instance, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 handles it like it’s nothing. You can have YouTube up in one corner while you check Messages for gift ideas and shop through the Amazon app. It might be helpful to keep a list of what you got and for whom in a floating Sheets window.

Industry observers note that the point is not only that it’s technically possible, but it’s usable. So often devices let users open apps in split screen, but are in no way comfortable enough for the task. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is perfect for it, and the experience actually makes you more productive, not less.

In a recent development, most phones don’t let you get the best angle without any sort of third-party accessory. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, though, acts like its own tripod in a way.

Let’s say you’re taking photos, and you need to get a shot of yourself, but no one is around to take the photo for you. The Galaxy Z Fold 8’s hinge lets it prop itself up, so you can do things like set a timer and run to strike a pose.

Industry observers note that this comes in handy for videos, too. Think of how many times you wanted to get a good angle on a plane or somewhere where there’s this flat surface just asking for a tiny tripod or kickstand. Well, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is its own kickstand and can be positioned at just the right angle.

Recent findings suggest that you can get the Galaxy Z Fold 8 from your favorite carriers and retailers, but Best Buy is one of the leading places to find deals during the holiday season. You’ll find hefty discounts, higher trade-in values for your old devices, and more.

Industry News: Maine Eyes Early 2027 Tribal iGaming Launch as Problem-Gambling Funding Draws Scrutiny

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (594 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readwrite

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing.
  • Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos.
  • Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maine's Gambling Control Unit is heading toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos after a single public hearing. A former lawmaker warns that the state's behavioral health system is too thin for a possible rise in gambling addiction, while a federal lawsuit still targets the tribes' exclusivity.

Maine’s regulator is moving toward an early 2027 launch of tribal-run online casinos. Only one public hearing has been held so far. WGME’s I-Team reported on Nov. 16 that the Gambling Control Unit began iGaming rulemaking in June. Residents in the report raised a separate concern. They worry the state lacks the mental health and problem-gambling resources to cope.

Maine will become the eighth state with legal online casinos. Its four Wabanaki tribes hold exclusive licenses under LD 1164, the Wabanaki internet gaming act. The Legislature lists the measure as enacted as Public Law 538.

Recent findings suggest that the money set aside for addiction services is small next to the state’s cut. The legislative fiscal note sends 2% of adjusted gross iGaming receipts to the Gambling Addiction Prevention and Treatment Fund. The state’s own 18% share is projected at $1.8 million in fiscal 2025-26 and $3.6 million in fiscal 2026-27.

Critics doubt the system can absorb the demand. Patty Locuratolo Hymanson, a neurologist and former state lawmaker, told WGME that Maine lacks the behavioral health resources to handle a possible rise in gambling addiction from online casinos.

Lawmakers reshaped the revenue split before passage. A committee amendment raised the state’s share from 16% to 18%. The same amendment cut the opioid treatment fund’s allocation from 3% to 1.5%. The fiscal note also carries ongoing General Fund appropriations of $645,354 for six Gambling Control Unit positions. Those include two criminal intelligence analysts and two auditors.

The regulator itself was skeptical at first. Before the bill became law, Executive Director Milt Champion opposed it in written testimony. He argued iGaming wasn’t warranted while sports wagering was only in its second year.

It has been revealed that rulemaking is still underway. The unit issued its third version of the draft rules on Sept. 30, 2026, and took comments until Oct. 30. Champion has warned that major revisions would force a fourth publication. The third draft keeps the tax rate on adjusted gross receipts unchanged. It also retains the license fee and bond requirements. The regulator is hiring six staff members dedicated to iGaming.

The launch also faces a court fight over tribal exclusivity. Churchill Downs and Oxford Casino Hotel brought their suit against the Gambling Control Unit and Champion in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maine. They are asking the court to declare the law unconstitutional. The challenge goes to the heart of the market’s design, which reserves online casino licenses for the tribes.

The next deadlines are procedural. Under Maine’s rulemaking law, the unit has up to 120 days after comments close to adopt the rules. The Attorney General’s office has up to 150 days from that same date to approve them as legal. The unit’s rulemaking page also lists a public hearing notice marked Nov. 30, 2026, which could change that timetable.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google has thoroughly redesigned Gemini for Android’s in-app camera that lets you swiftly add an image to prompts.

According to recent reports, available from the ‘plus’ menu in the prompt box, the old interface rolled out a fullscreen viewfinder that was quite generic. This UI is still in use when you launch the camera from the Gemini overlay.

The fresh one appears inline on the Gemini homepage or inside a conversation. It debuts as a bottom sheet that you can drag up — with a really slick animation — to take up most of the screen.

This nearly edge-to-edge redesign, which extends behind the system navigation bar, is a stark contrast to the old approach.

To the right of the capture button is a three-dot overflow button that animates on open, revealing options to control the flash and switch to the front-facing camera. There’s a back button on the other side, but you can also just swipe down.

This camera redesign first launched in the Gemini for iOS app, but has now widely rolled out on Android in both the beta and stable (version 17.76+) channels. Be sure to Force stop the Google app if you’re not seeing it live yet.

This follows the launch of GIF creation in the Gemini app yesterday. Powered by Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, select GIF from the Format menu or specify “Create a GIF” in your prompt. Google frames this feature as an alternative to searching for GIFs.

Say hello to GIFs in Gemini. Say goodbye to searching for the perfect one.From looping photo effects to funny memes, create any GIF you can imagine with our latest video model, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, for smooth motion and consistent quality across every frame.

According to recent reports, today, we’re excited to announce a deep-link integration between Hugging Face and Amazon SageMaker AI. Developers can now go from model discovery to hands-on experimentation in SageMaker Studio with a single selection. Whether you fine-tune a foundation model (FM) from Amazon SageMaker JumpStart or deploy it to an Amazon SageMaker Inference endpoint, you can now land directly inside the relevant SageMaker Studio workflow. Your selected model is pre-loaded, and the environment is fully configured and ready to go.

According to recent reports, previously, getting started on SageMaker Studio after discovering a model on Hugging Face required navigating multiple steps between opening Amazon SageMaker AI in the AWS Console, creating a domain, configuring IAM permissions, and sometimes requesting GPU quota. For developers who want to iterate quickly, this friction slows down the path from inspiration to experimentation. The integration creates a more direct path from discovery to enterprise deployment.

Industry observers note that “At Arcee, we build open models so developers and enterprises can actually own what they run: inspect the weights, post-train on their own data, and deploy on their own terms. This integration takes that promise the last mile. Going from an open model on Hugging Face straight into SageMaker Studio in a single click, then fine-tuning or deploying it inside your own AWS environment with nothing to wire up, is the kind of experience open models have been missing. Open weights you own, running in the cloud you control. That is exactly the combination our customers have been asking for.”.

— Mark McQuade, Founder and CEO, Arcee AI.

With the launch of a one-click Studio landing experience, choosing Customize on SageMaker AI or Deploy on SageMaker AI on a supported Hugging Face model page takes you directly to the console. SageMaker AI then automatically provisions a new domain with pre-configured permissions in seconds and carries the model context through.

This launch introduces three capabilities that shorten the path from a Hugging Face model to a working SageMaker Studio workflow.

When you browse models on Hugging Face, you’ll now see action buttons alongside supported models that map directly to SageMaker Studio workflows:.

Each entry point preserves the context, meaning you don’t need to search for the model again once inside Studio.

Fresh Studio environments created through this flow come with permissions already configured for the full range of SageMaker AI capabilities, including model customization, training jobs, notebook experimentation, and endpoint deployment. A new managed policy, AmazonSageMakerModelCustomizationCoreAccess, is created and attached for you. It provides permissions for serverless model customization jobs using supervised fine-tuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), and reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF), with supported deployment to SageMaker AI or Amazon Bedrock endpoints. This alleviates the need to manually create and configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles and policies before you can start experimenting. For existing Studio environments, actionable messages with direct links to documentation guide you through adding these permissions.

When selecting instance types for deployment or training, the Studio UI now surfaces quota availability directly in the instance selection list. You can immediately see which GPU instance types (G5, G6) are available under your account’s current limits. You don’t need to navigate separately to Service Quotas. If you still need to request a limit increase, you’re redirected directly to the Service Quotas page for the respective instance type.

Let’s walk through the experience of customizing or deploying a model starting from Hugging Face.

On the Hugging Face model page, click on “Deploy” and select “Amazon SageMaker AI”. If the model is supported, you will see two buttons, “Deploy on SageMaker AI” and “Customize on SageMaker AI”. Then select “Customize on SageMaker AI” for a supported model.

Industry observers note that you’re prompted to sign in to AWS using your existing credentials. If you already have an active console session, this step is skipped automatically. For more information, see Sign in to the AWS Management Console.

Recent findings suggest that you arrive directly on the Model Customization page inside SageMaker Studio with your model pre-selected. Next, configure your fine-tuning parameters such as training data, hyperparameters, and instance type, then submit the customization job.

It has been revealed that alternatively, selecting Deploy on SageMaker AI opens the endpoint deployment page in Studio with the model pre-configured. Select your instance type (quota visibility included), review the settings, and deploy.

After you deploy your endpoint, test inference directly from Studio’s endpoint testing interface.

You can try this experience today:.

It has been revealed that the launch of a one-click Studio landing experience minimizes the friction between discovering a model and experimenting with it. By connecting Hugging Face directly to the SageMaker Studio workflows, developers can stay in their flow. There’s no context switching, no manual environment setup, and no permission troubleshooting.

To get started, visit the Amazon SageMaker Studio page or explore models on Hugging Face and choose Deploy or Customize on SageMaker AI.

Converting Markdown to PDF is easy until the document has real content: long code blocks, wide tables, images and non-Latin text are where most tools fall apart.

Pandoc with LaTeX is still the most powerful route, but it needs a large install and trips over Unicode and emoji unless you switch engines and fonts.

Browser-based approaches (print CSS, Chromium-powered converters, in-browser tools) avoid the install and give you HTML-quality rendering, as long as you control page breaks.

A handful of print CSS rules (@page, break-inside: avoid, break-after: avoid) fix the majority of ugly PDFs, whichever tool you use.

Choose the tool by the document: a quick README export, a long technical report and a multilingual document each have a different best option.

Industry observers note that I write almost everything in Markdown: READMEs, release notes, client handovers, meeting notes. And at least once a week, someone asks for "the PDF version". Every time, the conversion looks fine on the first page and falls apart somewhere around page three: a code block split in half, a table running off the edge, an emoji replaced by an empty box.

In a recent development, sitePoint covered the classic route back in 2015 with Creating PDFs from Markdown with Pandoc and LaTeX. That approach still works. But a lot has changed since then, and today there are several ways to get a clean PDF without installing a TeX distribution. This article compares them, then goes through the rendering problems you'll actually hit, with a fix for each.

Pandoc is still the Swiss Army knife. The simplest command is:.

By default, that goes through LaTeX, which means you need a TeX distribution installed (several gigabytes for a full one). The output is beautiful for prose and math, but LaTeX has strong opinions about layout, and customizing it means writing LaTeX.

Pandoc can also render through an HTML engine instead, which lets you style the PDF with CSS:.

Best for: long documents, academic writing, math, automated pipelines.

Watch out for: install size, Unicode handling with the default engine (more on that below).

Render the Markdown to HTML (any previewer, a static site, a GitHub page) and print it to PDF. It's free and already installed everywhere, but you inherit whatever the page looks like on screen: navigation bars, sidebars, and page breaks wherever they happen to fall.

Best for: quick, one-off exports of short documents.

Watch out for: zero control over page breaks unless the page ships print CSS.

Extensions like Markdown PDF for VS Code, or CLI tools like md-to-pdf, render your Markdown to HTML and print it with a headless Chromium:.

You get the same rendering quality as a browser, plus a config file for CSS, margins, headers and footers. The trade-off is a Node install and a downloaded Chromium.

Best for: developers who live in their editor or want CI-friendly exports.

Watch out for: the first run downloads a browser, and print CSS is still your job.

Sources indicate that the newest option is tools that do the whole conversion inside the browser tab: you paste or drop the .md file, preview the actual pages and download the PDF. The good ones don't upload your file anywhere, which matters for client documents and internal notes.

Best for: people who don't want to install anything, non-developers on your team, private documents.

Watch out for: many online converters do upload your file to a server; check before you paste anything confidential.

Whichever method you pick, the same handful of problems show up as soon as the document is longer than a page. Most of them are fixed with print CSS, which works in Pandoc's HTML engines, Chromium-based tools and any HTML you print from a browser.

A 20-line function cut after line 3, with the rest on the next page, is the most common complaint. The fix is to ask the renderer not to break inside the block:.

Recent findings suggest that one caveat: a block longer than a full page has to break. For those, it's better to let it break cleanly than to push it to a latest page and leave a huge gap.

Sources indicate that on screen, a long line in a code block scrolls horizontally. On paper, there's no scrollbar, so it's simply cut off. Wrap long lines in print:.

According to recent reports, tables with many columns overflow the page or get squeezed until every cell is one word per line. Three things help: a smaller font size for tables, a landscape page for the worst offenders, and avoiding breaks in the middle of short tables:.

If a table genuinely needs eight columns, consider whether it should be a table in the PDF at all, or an appendix in landscape.

It has been revealed that A heading alone at the bottom of a page, with its content on the next one, looks broken. This rule keeps a heading attached to what follows it:.

Support for break-after: avoid varies between rendering engines, so test it with yours; when it isn't honored, a manual page break before the heading is the reliable fallback.

Markdown has no syntax for a page break. The usual trick is a raw HTML element that print CSS turns into a break:.

Some converters also recognize a comment like , which has the advantage of staying invisible when the same file is rendered on GitHub.

Images are inserted at their natural size, so a 4000-pixel screenshot spills off the page. Cap them:.

It has been revealed that for blurry images, the problem is usually the opposite: a small screenshot stretched to page width. Export screenshots at 2x if they're going into a PDF.

This one is specific to the LaTeX route. With the default pdflatex engine, Unicode characters outside its supported set produce errors or simply vanish. Switch to XeLaTeX or LuaLaTeX and give it a font that actually contains the characters:.

Sources indicate that emoji are harder still in LaTeX and often need a dedicated package. HTML-based renderers handle both far better, because they use the operating system's font fallback just like a web page does.

According to recent reports, internal links ([see setup](#setup)) and external links should stay clickable. HTML-based renderers usually keep both. If yours doesn't, check that headings get IDs (most Markdown parsers add them) and that the PDF engine preserves link annotations.

Put together, these rules make a solid starting point for any HTML-based route:.

Save it as print.css and pass it to Pandoc (--css=print.css with an HTML engine), to md-to-pdf through its config, or include it in the HTML you print from the browser.

My rule of thumb after a lot of trial and error:.

Industry observers note that A quick README or notes export, no install, private content: an in-browser converter. Full disclosure: this need is why I built the free Markdown to PDF converter on AwesomeToolkit, and it's what I use for this case now. It renders real A4 or Letter pages as you type, has an option to keep code blocks and tables whole, adds page numbers and a table of contents, and the conversion happens in the browser, so the file isn't uploaded anywhere.

Documentation in a repo, exported in CI: md-to-pdf or Pandoc with an HTML engine, plus the stylesheet above.

Long reports, math, academic formatting: Pandoc with XeLaTeX, using a font that covers every script in the document.

Something you'll print once and forget: the browser's Print to PDF is fine.

Whatever you choose, the biggest quality jump comes from the print rules, not the tool. Ten lines of CSS turn "it looks fine until page three" into a PDF you can actually send.

Yes. Your browser's Print to PDF works on any rendered Markdown, and in-browser converters do the whole conversion in a tab. Check that the converter processes files locally if the content is private.

The default pdflatex engine has limited Unicode support. Use --pdf-engine=xelatex or lualatex and set a font that contains the characters with -V mainfont= (and -V CJKmainfont= for CJK text).

Recent findings suggest that markdown has no native syntax for it. Insert where you want the break, or use the page-break comment your converter supports.

Add pre { break-inside: avoid; } to your print CSS. Blocks longer than a page will still break, which is expected.

Industry observers note that with HTML-based renderers, usually yes, both external links and links to headings inside the document. Test internal links in particular, since they depend on headings having IDs.

Recent findings suggest that walmart has the ABS Cyclone M Aqua on sale for just $750, which is a prebuilt that packs an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4 memory, and a 1TB SSD. ABS is Newegg's in-house PC brand, and yet Walmart is the only retailer where we found this deal.

According to recent reports, just about any gaming PC you find under $1,000 has some serious compromises given the ongoing RAM, SSD, and GPU pricing crisis's. And this machine too has compromises, notably with the mATX motherboard and single 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM. You're getting a lot for the money even with those compromises between the Core i5-14400F and RTX 5060, however. As you can see from our roundup of the best Black Friday gaming PC deals, there aren't a ton of options at this price. And in our tracking of Black Friday GPU deals, we found that the RTX 5060 is selling for close to $500 in many cases.

The ABS Cyclone M Aqua is an mATX prebuilt with an RTX 5060, Core i5-14400F, 16GB of DDR4, and a 1TB NVMe SSD.

As you can see from the data from our GPU benchmark hierarchy, the RTX 5060 is a graphics card that's most comfortable at 1080p, though it can scale up to 1440p, assuming you're willing to lean into Nvidia's DLSS suite between Super Resolution and Multi-Frame Generation, both of which are supported on this GPU.

Its main limitation is the 8GB frame buffer, which could pose problems in some titles at 1440p. For the vast majority of 1080p games, it shouldn't be a problem. In our testing of DLSS 5, which is supported on the RTX 5060, we found that the 8GB frame buffer posed a limitation on performance. However, Nvidia has already apparently slashed the VRAM usage of its DLSS 5 model. The RTX 5060 was fast enough to reach 58 FPS at 1080p with DLSS 5 still.

Outside of the GPU, the Core i5-14400F is the perfect CPU for a rig like this. It provides performance on the level of the Core i5-14600K in games while sacrificing a bit of peak productivity power and the unlocked multiplier.

The one major downside with this configuration is the single 16GB DDR4-3200 DIMM. With just a single stick, your bandwidth is cut in half. Thankfully, the motherboard has four DIMM slots, so you can add another 16GB module to double your capacity and unlock the full bandwidth. Thankfully, DDR4 is much cheaper than DDR5, as you can see in our RAM price tracker.

The RGB is a little less OTT than other models, though, instead going for a classic, rather understated design. It's a magnetic board, too, with magnetic hot-swappable switches.

It has been revealed that jump into the future of keyboards on the cheap (for Hall Effect) with the Keychron K10 HE full-size keyboard. Priced at $115.99, you'd be hard-pressed to find a better deal on full-size Hall Effect keyboard.

You're getting double-shot PBT keycaps here, and underneath them are Gateron double-rail magnetic switches. These give you a lightening-fast response time with a 0.1mm press sensitivity, along with adjustable actuation points for per-key customization. This gives you full flexibility over the entire board.

In a recent development, you've got two options on sale, with the all-black and all-white options at the same $115.99 price: a great deal on a full-size Hall effect keyboard. — Ben Stockton.

In a recent development, anker has carved a name for itself in the portable power bank business, and it's a familiar option for Amazon buyers. Right now, you can pick up its laptop power bank, with a huge 25,000 mAh battery capacity, for just $91.19. That's a 32% discount compared to its usual list price.

The Anker Laptop Power Bank can supply up to 165 watts when two USB-C ports are in use. It also features a retractable USB-C cable and another integrated cable that doubles as a carrying strap.

Industry observers note that $91 is enough to get you a power bank with three USB-C ports, including one retractable cable, each capable of 100W each, with a USB-A port capable of 33W. If you're using more than one USB-C cable, you can output a maximum of 165W between them or 133W if you’re using one USB-C port and the USB-A port. If you max out the power bank by using all four ports simultaneously, you’re limited to 130 watts maximum output.

This will let you power up a smartphone, laptop, portable game console, and more, with up to 100W each to supported devices. If your laptop can push that far, it'll carry on charging your laptop until it depletes. It's also capable of charging up itself with a 100W-charger, gaining 30% in 22 minutes.

Industry observers note that there's also a built-in display that lets you see charge, device temperature and battery health. If you're on-the-go with plenty of devices in your bag, this is the kind of battery pack you'll want at your disposal. — Ben Stockton.

Our favorite gaming chair isn't a typical racing-style chair, but it's not an office one, either. It's this collab between Herman Miller and Logitech G. The Vantum, ergonomic but "built for gamers" with gaming features like an adjustable neckrest, lumbar support and forward-leaning alignment is on sale right now for $768.07 right now, down from $1,155, with an extra 5% off thanks to a Black Friday promo code.

Features an "active, forward leaning alignment," adjustable lumbar support, and passively-adaptive thoracic support. It has a foam-padded seat cushion and a mesh suspension backrest for breathability, as well as an adjustable neck rest.

Use code SAVE5 for 5% extra off.

In a recent development, the Vantum is a seriously premium chair. It has a mesh backrest and a padded cushioned seat, along with 4D armrests with padding. As you can imagine, it scored well in our Herman Miller x Logitech G Vantum review, thanks to its lightweight but comfortable design, with the adjustable lumbar support similar to the functionality you'd see in the firm's pricier Herman Miller task chairs.

While the chair doesn't offer full recline, its tilt mechanism is pretty comfortable, as is the passively-adaptive thoracic support. This Black Friday discount means you can save $386.93, as long as you use the SAVE5 code at checkout to get the full discount. — Ben Stockton.

Industry observers note that the Logitech Yeti Orb is the spiritual successor to the classic Blue Snowball microphone — it's a unique-looking, ball-shaped microphone that sits on top of a sturdy desktop tripod stand and sounds great out of the box. It's our favorite budget-priced gaming mic and it's on sale right now for an even more budget-friendly $39.99 at Best Buy — $30 off its MSRP of $69.99.

This round, ball-shaped desktop mic features a cardioid polar pattern and sounds great out of the box. It comes with a desktop stand and has customizable RGB lighting, and can be mounted at two different angles.

Industry observers note that the Yeti Orb is a simple, stylish microphone that comes with a plastic desktop tripod stand in the box. It has the Blue Snowball's iconic ball shape, with two mounting points — so you can mount it straight on, or at an angle, depending on whether you're mounting it on the included stand or on a boom arm. There are no on-mic controls or ports (other than its USB-C port), so you won't be able to adjust the mic's gain or plug in a headset for zero-latency monitoring, and for that reason it's not really a mic for serious streamers. But it does have customizable RGB lighting, which indicates whether the mic is recording, and it sounds great right out of the box — so while you can tweak the settings using Logitech G Hub (which comes with Blue Vo!ce), you don't have to. It's a great mic for casual chatting and streaming, and this is a great price to get it at. You can read my full review of the Logitech Yeti Orb here. — Sarah.

Corsair's wireless MMO / MOBA-focused gaming mouse features 16 programmable buttons, including 12 in a side array, and sports Corsair's 33K Marksman S optical sensor. It also has native integration with Elgato's Stream Deck platform, so you can map Stream Deck commands directly to the buttons.

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a mouse with tons of buttons, look no further than Corsair's Scimitar line — the Corsair Scimitar Elite SE Wireless is currently on sale for just $69.99 at Best Buy, which is 50% off its retail price of $139.99. And if you don't need a wireless mouse, the wired Corsair Scimitar RGB Elite is down to $49.99 at Amazon, which is 44% off its retail price of $89.99.

The Scimitar RGB Elite mouse from Corsair features 17 programmable buttons, including 12 located on the side panel, the left/right primary mouse buttons, two DPI switch buttons above the scroll wheel, and the scroll wheel's center click. You can slide the 12-button side panel to fit your hand size.

The Corsair Scimitar Elite SE Wireless is an MMO / MOBA-focused gaming mouse with an adjustable 12-button side panel — it doesn't swap out, like the side panel on the Razer Naga V2 / V3 Pro, but it does move forward and back (it comes with a hex tool so you can adjust it to where you want and lock it in). It doesn't move a ton, but it's a nice accommodation for people who find that the giant gaming mice that dominate the market don't have buttons in quite the right places.

The Scimitar Elite SE Wireless sports Corsair's Marksman S 33K sensor, which has a maximum resolution of 33,000 DPI and a maximum speed of 750 IPS and can handle up to 50 G's of force. It's a heavier mouse — 4.02oz / 114g, but weight isn't that big of a deal in the MMO / MOBA community. Also, it's integrated with Elgato's Stream Deck platform, so you can program Stream Deck functionality directly to the mouse's buttons. You can read my full review of the Corsair Scimitar Elite SE Wireless here. — Sarah.

The 9800X3D might not be the fastest gaming CPU on the market but it's still the best option owing to its speed and power draw. Now, at Amazon, it just crashed to an all-time low of $369, thanks to a coupon you can apply before checking out.

The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is a potent gaming 8-core, 16-thread desktop CPU. It has a massive 96MB L3 cache for gaming performance, with clock speeds of up to 5.2GHz.

In a recent development, the 9800X3D really needs no introduction, but in case you aren't familiar, this is one the best gaming CPUs around. IT isn't quite AMD's fastest — the 9850X3D takes that crown — but this chip draws significantly less power while still being very close in terms of performance. The industry leading 3D V-Cache means the CPU is much less reliant on your slower RAM, drastically boosting frame rates.

This deal is not likely to be around for long, so move fast if you want one to start an AM5 build or upgrade your existing rig. - Stephen Warwick.

This TKL mechanical keyboard features hot-swappable switches and a built-in Stream Deck with 12 LCD keys, a 2.75-inch screen, and 2 rotary knobs.

In a recent development, the Corsair Galleon 100 SD is a keyboard with an integrated Stream Deck — it's a mechanical keyboard with a TKL layout, plus a 2-knob, 12-key Stream Deck that has all the functionality of Elgato's Stream Deck platform. Although I still lament the lack of a true 10-key numberpad, I have to admit that the Corsair Galleon 100 SD has been my daily driver for the better part of the past year. Who knew an integrated Stream Deck was so useful?!

Of course, at $350... it's definitely not cheap. But right now it's down to $259.99 at Best Buy — $90 off its retail price, and a pretty good deal when you consider you're getting both a keyboard and a Stream Deck in one.

Sources indicate that the Galleon 100 SD is a pretty premium keyboard, with a nice-looking design, double-shot PBT keycaps, a pass-through USB port, and a hot-swappable PCB. It comes with only one switch option: Corsair's MLX Pulse (purple) switches, which are "thocky and linear" — and they sound pretty good, though they're definitely linear. The case has six layers of sound-dampening foam and it's a great-sounding keyboard overall, especially for a mainstream gaming keyboard.

According to recent reports, the Stream Deck features 12 LCD keys that are the same size and shape as typical Stream Deck keys. There's a 2.75-inch LCD screen above the keys, which is divided into quadrants that are controlled by the two notched, clickable rotary knobs at the top. The Stream Deck is a true Stream Deck, so it has all the functionality of Elgato's platform, and can be easily programmed with the Stream Deck software. The keyboard also comes with a soft-touch plastic wrist rest, two USB cables, and a handful of other accessories in the box. You can read my full review of the Corsair Galleon 100 SD here. — Sarah.

Recent findings suggest that the Turtle Beach Atlas Air lives up to its name — this wireless, open-back headset is lightweight and airy in both comfort and sound. Although its all-plastic design didn't feel quite up to the $179.99 price point it debuted at, the comfort and audio quality was enough for us to recommend it — and now it's down to just $119.99 at Amazon for Black Friday.

In a recent development, the only wireless open-back gaming headset on the market is incredibly light and comfortable and sounds great. It has a detachable, flip-to-mute boom mic, dual-mode wireless connectivity, and gets about 50 hours of battery life.

Sources indicate that the Atlas Air is a wireless, open-back headset, which means the sound isn't closed in. While this does mean that people around you can hear what you're listening to, there are several benefits to an open-back design — specifically, you don't get the same listening fatigue you get when listening to a closed-back headset, because the sound can escape instead of reverberating inside your head. For gamers, it also allows for a wider soundstage and a more immersive environment. As long as you don't work in close quarters, an open-back headset is a nice option if you don't want to commit to speakers.

Industry observers note that the Atlas Air has a lightweight, plastic build, with a mesh suspension headband and floating earcups. It's extremely lightweight — just 10.61oz / 301g — and it basically feels like you're wearing nothing. It sports 40mm dynamic drivers with a frequency response range of 20 - 40,000 Hz, and it sounds surprisingly good: it has a nice, wide soundstage and a slightly bass-heavy sound profile, and it did especially well with picking up details in layered audio environments, such as cities and jungles. It's probably not the headset for those looking to gain advantage in shooting games — the directional sound is fine, but a closed-back headset will help you zero in on footsteps and gunshots. But for the less competitive games, this is a great option, especially if you find other headsets hard to wear for long periods of time. You can read my full review of the Atlas Air here. — Sarah.

The Razer Naga V2 Pro is one of my favorite mice of all time, because I can never have enough buttons on a mouse. This wireless mouse is aimed at MMO / MOBA players, but it can actually be used by just about anyone thanks to the three swappable side plates it comes bundled with. Naturally, this kind of versatility doesn't come cheap, but right now you can grab the Naga V2 Pro for just $129.99 at Amazon — $50 off its MSRP of $179.99.

The Razer Naga V2 Pro sports a customizable magnetic side plate, offering 12-, 6-, and 2-button configurations, Razer's Hyperscroll Pro wheel, fully wireless connectivity, and its Focus Pro 30K Optical sensor.

The Naga V2 Pro comes with three interchangeable side plates with 12-, 6-, and 2-button configurations. It's not the lightest mouse on the market — it weighs 4.72oz / 134g, but lightness is not what most MMO players are looking for. Instead, they're looking for comfort, and the Naga V2 Pro is a very comfortable mouse, with a contoured, ergonomic right-handed shape and a rest for your ring finger. It sports Razer's Focus Pro 30K optical sensor, which has a maximum sensitivity of 30,000 DPI and a maximum speed of 750 IPS and can handle up to 70 G's of acceleration. It also has a customizable tilt wheel, which can be tuned in Razer's Synapse software.

Recent findings suggest that I used this mouse for two years straight, until I recently replaced it with the Razer Naga V3 Pro — more because my Naga V2 Pro was starting to look a little worse for the wear, not because it wasn't still a fantastic mouse. You can read my full review of the Razer Naga V2 Pro here. — Sarah.

According to recent reports, the HyperX Cloud III wired gaming headset is one of the most comfortable headsets we've ever tested — it's almost exactly the same as the HyperX Cloud III S Wireless, just, well, wired. It has a premium build with a steel headband and curved aluminum forks, large over-ear earcups with leatherette-covered memory foam padding, and a leatherette-covered padded headband. It's sleek and understated, with a detachable boom microphone, and it's fairly lightweight at just 10.86oz / 308g. And it's currently on sale for $39 at Walmart — down $60.99 from its MSRP of $99.99.

It has been revealed that the HyperX Cloud III is a wired gaming headset with a detachable microphone. It features 53mm drivers and virtual surround sound support.

Industry observers note that the Cloud III wired gaming headset is basically the most comfortable headset we've tested in recent years. It's fairly adjustable, with earcups that tilt and are independently height-adjustable (they don't pivot, but the forks allow for some lateral movement and the headband is very flexible). The memory foam padding is thick and soft enough to wear comfortably over glasses, and the clamping force is practically perfect — enough that it won't fall off if you tilt your head back, but not much stronger than that. Add this into the weight and you have a headset that you can wear for hours and hours at a time without needing a break.

The headset sports HyperX's angled 53mm dynamic drivers, which have a frequency response range of 10 - 21,000 Hz — slightly outside the typical frequency response range of most gaming headsets, and nicely tuned to give you a neutral audio profile that still brings plenty of bass. This is the wired version, and it comes with an analog cable that can plug into a USB cable extension, which gives you plenty of length for when you're sitting at a PC while still being able to plug into any standard 3.5mm jack. It was already a good deal at its starting $100 price point, and at $39 it's absolutely worth it.

You can read my full review of the HyperX Cloud III wired gaming headset here. — Sarah.

Whether you were a Mac fan in the late 90s or not, there’s a whole lot of nostalgia in this design. It’s available in four colors and is right now 50% off, taking it down to $19.99 at Amazon.

This ABS plastic Mac Mini case is pure nostalgia and not all that practical, but there are benefits to tipping Apple’s smallest Mac up on its side.

Aside from the throwback 90s looks, tipping the Mac Mini on its side like this actually lets you press the power button without lifting up the mini PC. Plus, if your desk space is cramped, putting the system on its side will free up some room. -- Matt Safford.

If you're in the market for a current-gen RTX 50-series card that won't set you back thousands of dollars, then this might be the deal for you. Newegg is selling the cheapest RTX 5060 you can buy right now at $439.99, an $80 saving. While that's a far cry from the MSRP of $299, GPUs are very expensive these days, so this is about as good as it gets for 1080p gaming.

Get an RTX 5060 with 8GB of GDDR7 VRAM, clock speeds of 2550 MHz, 3840 CUDA cores, and a free GPU holder.

Recent findings suggest that at 1080p, the RTX 5060 can put out more than 60 fps, making it perfect for entry-level gaming. It also supports Nvidia's DLSS technologies, so you can squeeze out more frames or even try your hand at 1440p.

This specific version of the RTX 5060 is Zotac's AMP series, with core clocks of 2550 MHz, with the same speed listed for its boost clocks. It has 3840 CUDA cores, and 8GB of GDDR7 VRAM with a 128-bit memory interface. While this won't blow titles out of the water at 4K, this is budget gaming performance at a time when GPUs are becoming increasingly more expensive. - Stephen Warwick.

Buying a PC on Black Friday doesn't have to mean spending the Earth. If you want a budget build, this Intel Core i7 14700F rig from Cyberpower is a fantastic cheap option for 1080p gaming. With an RTX 5060 Ti 8GB, this should be brilliant for entry-level gaming and could even be pushed to 1440p with Nvidia's DLSS technology.

The CyberPower Gamer Xtreme prebuilt PC offers a 20-Core Intel i7 14700F CPU, RTX 5060 Ti GPU, 16GB of DDR5 memory, and 1 TB of storage, wrapped up in a white case, and flush with glowing RGB fans.

According to recent reports, as you can see from our testing data, in our 19-game testing suite, the RTX 5060 Ti 8GB is good for average frame rates of 72 fps. This drops to around 46 at 1440p without any help from frame generation.

The CPU in this build is Intel's i7 14700F with 20 cores and 28 threads, boasting boost clocks of up to 5.4 GHz- a great processor for productivity and gaming.

Aside from the potent 20-core CPU and GPU for 1080, you also get 16GB of DDR5 RAM and a 1TB SSD. Windows 11 Home comes as standard, and the motherboard supports Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth 5.3. There are also ports aplenty. - Stephen Warwick.

Sources indicate that samsung's P9 Express microSDXC is one of the top storage solutions for Nintendo Switch 2. With transfer speeds of up to 800 MB/s and similar sequential read speeds, this is a speedy storage solution for your handheld.

The Switch 2 ships with 256GB of internal storage as standard, so a 512GB expansion will triple that capacity for storing games and files. While not quite its lowest-ever price, there's a great deal on this card, 38% off at Amazon, now just $92.99.

The Samsung P9 is a microSD Express card that offers great performance and reliability for its price. The 512GB model is presently priced at its original MSRP of $99.99.

The P9 Express comes with Dynamic Thermal Guard technology to stop your card from overheating while in use for smoother gameplay. It also has a three-year warranty and can be used with microSD UHS-I devices such as tablets and drones, too.

The 256GB model is also on sale, an arguably better value. At 44% off, it's less than half the price of the 512GB model. In theory, buying two would get you the same amount of storage for $89, provided you don't mind swapping cards around.

According to recent reports, the Samsung P9 is a microSD Express card that offers great performance and reliability for its price. The 256GB model is currently priced at its original MSRP of $44.99.

Industry observers note that with SSD and flash storage prices through the roof thanks to AI, this is a solid deal on a great Nintendo Switch 2 card. - Stephen Warwick.

I use the Gateron Oil King Ghost Pro switches on my own keyboard, and they're a go-to linear switch for a good reason. The heavier 50gf operating force is heavier than a standard Red-style switch, leading to a deep sound and more pronounced feedback while typing, particularly if you're a heavy typer.

The Oil King Ghost Pro switches are linear key switches for a mechanical keyboard with a 50gf operating force.

These switches are an upgraded version of standard Oil Kings, with the upcoming Ghost name noting the passthrough channel for lighting. The switches themselves are the same, and they come factory lubricated, so they sound great out of the box. You can use the switches with any standard 3-pin or 5-pin PCB — Jake Roach.

It has been revealed that this hefty Lenovo Legion gaming laptop is the first RTX 5090-powered laptop we've seen under $4,000. This is a huge spec with a 240Hz OLED display, 24GB VRAM GPU, a massive 24-core Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX CPU, 32GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD.

Sources indicate that the 16-inch Lenovo Legion Pro 7i gaming laptop comes with an Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus CPU, RTX 5090 (175W TGP) GPU, 32GB of DDR5 memory, and 1TB of storage. The OLED display offers a 240Hz refresh rate and a 2560 x 1600 resolution.

With its 24 cores and performance core boost clocks of up to 5.5 GHz, this is a fantastic mobile CPU for both work and play. Combined with the laptop RTX 5090, the best laptop GPU on the market, this will make light work of any title you can throw at it in the 2560 x 1200 resolution. That stunning OLED will really make games pop, too.

Also offers 1x Thunderbolt 4 port (USB-C), 1x 3.2 Gen 2 (USB-C), 1x USB 3.2 Gen 2 (USB-A), 2x USB 3.2 Gen 1 (USB-A), a 3.5mm headphone jack, 1x HDMI 2.1 port, and a 2.5 Gbps Ethernet jack, as well as Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 5.4. While we haven't reviewed this specific spec, in our Lenovo Legion Pro 7i Gen 10 review, the laptop scored very well thanks to its exceptional OLED screen, aluminum chassis, and sharp webcam. - Stephen Warwick.

Industry observers note that earlier this week, we highlighted a great deal on Apple's MacBook Neo, which is $100 off and back to its original launch price of $599. This is also better than the previous $50 discount to $649, so if you missed out the first time, this deal is now better! The $599 price gets you 256GB of storage and 8GB of RAM, and is available in all four of Apple's vibrant colors.

You can also snag the 512GB version for $699, a $100 discount.

Recent findings suggest that apple's base MacBook Neo has an A18 Pro chip, 256GB of storage, and 8GB of RAM. A solid alternative with a more powerful SoC.

Recent findings suggest that the A18 Pro chip in the MacBook Neo is solid for single-core productivity performance excelling in single-core performance, though the 8GB can be difficult for serious multitasking. For people working on basic tasks, this is going to be sufficient.There have been a handful of other deals on the Neo so far this week. We saw the base model drop to $599 (in citrus only) at one point, while the upgraded 512GB model with Touch ID dropped to $699 (in blush) at another. It's possible we'll see more color-specific price drops, but it's not a guarantee, and $649 isn't bad given the RAM situation. — Andrew E. Freedman.

In a recent development, in what might be one of the best gaming PC deals we've seen so far, this HyperX OMEN desktop at Best Buy, featuring Intel's Core Ultra 7 270K Plus and RTX 5080 GPU, is now just $2,699. The graphics card in this build alone presently retails for around $1,700, making this a really good value build.

Get an RTX 5080 PC with Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 16GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, with plenty of space to upgrade. Also features Wi-Fi 7.

The star of the show here is the RTX 5080, a fully-fledged 4K GPU that will take care of any title you want to play at high resolutions and settings. That's complemented by the Intel Core Ultra 7 270K, a much-improved Intel gaming CPU released not too long ago. With 24 cores, it performs extremely well in productivity tasks as well as gaming. While it can't quite match the X3D SKUs of AMD for gaming performance, it is still a very strong desktop CPU.

The supporting cast of the build is perhaps the only compromise. The 1TB SSD is fine to get you started, but 16GB of RAM is a little less than we'd like in a build of this caliber. Still, this is such a cheap build for an RTX 5080 that it will be worth the trade-off for some. Of course, if you already have some DDR5 RAM lying around, you could swap that in, or you could spend some of that $1,700 saving on an upgrade.

The build supports up to 128GB of memory, with 4 DIMM slots for future expansion. It also has two further SSD slots, as well as Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0, thanks to the Intel Z890 motherboard inside.

Recent findings suggest that this build will not be around for long, so move fast if you want to grab one. - Stephen Warwick.

Whether you need to upgrade your boot drive or you’re attempting to rescue the laptop or gaming PC of a friend or family member, an SSD cloner can make a scary, potentially tedious job surprisingly easy. I know because I bought this cloner a couple of years ago (when it cost about $15 more) and moved someone’s existing OS from an extremely cramped 128GB drive onto a faster 512GB drive in less than half an hour. And now Rosewill’s SSD cloner is on sale for its lowest-ever price at Amazon.

With support for NVMe M.2 SSDs and offline cloning, this handy device makes it simple to move your files or OS from one drive to another. And with a 20 Gbps USB-C interface, it's also speedy in your OS of choice if you want to use software to clone or move your data between drives.

Keep in mind this device only supports M Key PCIe / NVMe drives, so it won’t work with SATA M.2 drives. But it can work both as a standalone drive or with software if you need to, say, resize the partition. The Rosewill cloner is also handy for checking the contents of M.2 drives you may have lying around. But if that's all you need, you can get a good tool-free enclosure for less than $20. -- Matt Safford.

Nothing confirms ‘aggressive’ smartphone release schedule for 2027 with US focus

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alongside a teaser for the new Ear (note) recorder, Nothing CEO Carl Pei has confirmed the firm’s aims for a major 2027 in terms of smartphone releases, as well as a focus on the US market.
  • Speaking to Bloomberg, Carl Pei says that Nothing currently has “tens of millions of devices in use,” and that there are major plans for 2027.
  • This includes “more attention” to the US market for Nothing, with the US being Nothing’s fastest-growing market for audio devices.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alongside a teaser for the new Ear (note) recorder, Nothing CEO Carl Pei has confirmed the firm’s aims for a major 2027 in terms of smartphone releases, as well as a focus on the US market.

Speaking to Bloomberg, Carl Pei says that Nothing currently has “tens of millions of devices in use,” and that there are major plans for 2027.

This includes “more attention” to the US market for Nothing, with the US being Nothing’s fastest-growing market for audio devices. In 2026, Nothing introduced its Ear (3a) earbuds, multiple CMF-branded devices, and two pairs of over-ear headphones including its high-end Headphone (1) Pro in September, all of which are sold in the US (and on sale during Black Friday).

Pei further noted that Nothing would have a more “aggressive” smartphone release schedule in 2027. Previously, it was said that Nothing would launch six latest smartphones next year, following just three new smartphones in 2026.

In a recent development, pei noted Nothing now has “tens of millions of devices in use” across its smartphones, earbuds and other products. The company is also planning to devote more attention to the US market, while pursuing a more aggressive smartphone release schedule next year than it did in 2026.

The tech giant noted it has generated more than $2 billion in revenue since its first product release in 2022 and that the US is its fastest growing market for audio gear.

According to recent reports, nothing doesn’t have a strict schedule for upcoming product rolls out, but Nothing Phone (4a) debuted in March 2026, with Phone (3) launching in the Summer of the year prior. With six new devices supposedly in the works, it’s anyone’s guess as to when they might release.
